extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental chemists, and scholars evaluating chemical/hypothesis reasoning (early modern context)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for assessing chemical (chymical) hypotheses, the probative value of experiments (especially analyses by fire), and the explanatory adequacy of proposed principles (e.g., the Tria Prima or four elements). Emphasizes empirical demonstration, scope, consistency, and caution against overgeneralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Skepticism that fire is the universal resolver
rubrics_metrics.description: Since, in the first place, it may justly be doubted whether or no the Fire be, as Chymists suppose it, the genuine and Universal Resolver of mixt Bodies
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept as given that heating (the 'fire') necessarily reveals original elemental constituents. Experimental evidence must support that fire truly resolves a compound into its pre‑existing components rather than producing new products or artifacts of the process. Anti‑pattern: treating the mere production of distinct substances on heating as proof that the fire has revealed original elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof required that separated substances were pre-existent
rubrics_metrics.description: we may doubt ... whether or no all the Distinct Substances that may be obtain'd from a mixt body by the Fire were pre-existent there in the formes in which they were separated from it
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When substances are obtained by analysis, demand demonstration that each separated product existed in that form prior to the analysis. Experiments should distinguish between separation of pre‑existing constituents and production of new compounds by the analytic procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency of the number of components across cases
rubrics_metrics.description: the Number of such substances does not appear the same in all mixt Bodies; some of them being Resoluble into more differing substances than three, and Others not being Resoluble into so many as three
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A general theory that postulates a fixed number of principles (e.g., three or five) must be supported by consistent observations across many kinds of bodies. Avoid generalizing from a few examples when the number and kinds of products vary by specimen.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separated products are often themselves mixts, not pure elements
rubrics_metrics.description: those very substances that are thus separated are not for the most part pure and Elementary bodies, but new kinds of mixts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat separation products with caution: they may be complex or compounded rather than elemental. Methodological implication: further analysis and characterization are needed before labeling a product 'elementary.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not infer identical nature from a single shared quality
rubrics_metrics.description: it will be but somewhat a gross Way of judging of the Nature of Bodies, to conclude without Scruple, that those must be of the same Nature that agree in some such General Quality, as Fluidity, Dryness, Volatility, and the like
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid inferring that two bodies are of the same kind simply because they share one general property (e.g., volatility, dryness). Examples: calxes of gold, vitriol, talc, and common ashes may all be dry, yet differ greatly in nature. A robust identification requires multiple converging properties and careful analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explanatory scope must account for variety of textures and consistences
rubrics_metrics.description: how great Variety there is in the Textures and Consistences of Compound Bodie; and how little the consistence and Duration of many of them seem to accommodate and be explicable by the propos'd Notion
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A satisfactory theory should explain diverse phenomena such as texture, consistence, durability, and difference in behavior under heat. Anti‑pattern: a narrow hypothesis that accounts only for a subset of observations (e.g., exterior crust bodies) while failing for others (e.g., glass from ashes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize experimental evidence over speculative reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: I declar'd to you that I would at this Conference Examine only the Experiments of my Adversaries, not their Speculative Reasons
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating a doctrine, focus first on the strength and interpretation of experiments rather than on speculative metaphysical explanations. Use empirical results to constrain or falsify speculative frameworks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument from shared qualities to a common principle is precarious
rubrics_metrics.description: Ubicunque pluribus eædem affectiones & qualitates insunt, per commune quoddam Principium insint ... the Argumentation ... is built upon a precarious supposition
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skeptically assess inferences that because many bodies share qualities (colors, odors, tastes) they therefore share a single underlying principle. Demand demonstration that such qualities necessarily arise from the same subject rather than from different causes or combinations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Internal consistency and non‑redundancy of explanatory categories
rubrics_metrics.description: they both derive several qualities from the same Principle, and must ascribe the same quality to almost all their Principles and other bodies besides
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A good explanatory framework should not inconsistently assign the same quality to multiple distinct principles nor attribute many different qualities to a single principle without justification. Inconsistency and redundancy indicate weak theoretical structure and should prompt reconsideration or refinement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental methods must unambiguously isolate elements (ocular demonstration)
rubrics_metrics.description: when he comes to make good his confident Undertaking, to give us an occular Demonstration of the immediate Presence of the four Elements in the resolution of Green Wood, He is fain to say things that agree very little with one another
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims that an experimental procedure shows the presence of elementary substances require clear, reproducible, and unambiguous demonstrations. Beware of ambiguous operational signs (e.g., mistaking condensable droplets for 'air') and of experiments whose different readings contradict each other.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not overextend conclusions beyond the domain of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: how narrow is this Philosophy, that reaches but to some of those compound Bodies, which we find but upon, or in the crust or outside of our terrestrial Globe ... what does it teach us ... of the Sun ... or the fixt Starrs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid extrapolating a hypothesis supported in a limited domain (e.g., terrestrial compounds) to vastly different domains (e.g., celestial bodies) without supporting data. Keep scope claims proportionate to the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account for widely distributed general properties
rubrics_metrics.description: I shall demand, upon what Chymical Principle Fluidity depends? ... I might ask the like Question concerning Light ... in which of the three Principles the Quality, we call Sound, resides
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theoretical principles should be able to address highly general properties (fluidity, motion, light, sound) or else explain why those properties lie outside their remit. It is problematic to claim limited principles when such broad properties appear across many kinds of bodies and scales.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider microstructure and texture when explaining macroscopic properties
rubrics_metrics.description: the Differing Gravity of Bodies proceeds chiefly from their particular Texture, as is manifest in Gold, the closest and Compactest of Bodies, which is many times heavier
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explanations for macroscopic behaviors (weight, density, fluidity) should incorporate the role of minute parts and texture, not rely solely on assignment to an elemental category. Empirical measures of microstructure can be decisive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish experimental artifacts from genuine qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: that their Saline Tast is only an Effect of Incineration and Adustion, it has been elsewhere fully reply'd ... when we refine Gold and Silver, the violentest Fires We can Employ on them give them not the least Rellish of Saltness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control for process‑induced changes: tasting, residues, or properties produced by incineration/distillation may be artifacts of the method or contaminants. Require controls and comparative procedures to attribute a quality to the substance rather than to the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value experimental contributions independently of contested theories
rubrics_metrics.description: when I acknowledg the usefulness of the Labours of Spagyrists to Natural Philosophy, I do it upon the score of their experiments, not upon that of Their Speculations
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain and use reliable empirical results even if the theoretical interpretation offered by their authors is questionable. Separate empirical practice from speculative doctrine; experimental methods and data can advance knowledge regardless of adherence to a particular theoretical framework.
